rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Protozoa are animal-like, mostly unicellular eukaryotes classified by their locomotion into four classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia, e.g. Amoeba), Mastigophora (flagella, e.g. Trypanosoma), Ciliophora (cilia, e.g. Paramecium), and Sporozoa (non-motile spores, e.g. Plasmodium). Paramecium and Amoeba are model organisms. Plasmodium (malaria) with its Anopheles vector is a key NEB examination topic.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Protozoa classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia), Mastigophora (flagella), Ciliophora (cilia), Sporozoa (spores/non-motile)
Amoeba: cell membrane + cytoplasm + nucleus + food vacuole + contractile vacuole
Paramecium: cilia + oral groove + food vacuole + macro/micronucleus + contractile vacuole

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Protista is a single group of organisms.** — Protista is a polyphyletic kingdom-level group; it contains very diverse organisms (algae, protozoa, slime moulds) that are grouped together mainly because they are unicellular eukaryotes, not because they share close evolutionary relationships.  ·  **Binary fission and conjugation in Paramecium are both reproduction.** — Binary fission is asexual reproduction producing new individuals. Conjugation is a sexual process for genetic exchange between two individuals; it does not increase the number of organisms and is therefore NOT reproduction.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled Paramecium diagram and the 4-class Protozoa table.  ·  Plasmodium life cycle (human + mosquito) with Anopheles vector is a very frequent long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Amoeba proteus — Sarcodina; pseudopodia; no fixed shape.  ·  Paramecium caudatum — Ciliophora; cilia; two nuclei; oral groove.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Protista:** unicellular eukaryotes. Includes protozoa (animal-like), algae (plant-like) and slime moulds (fungus-like).  ·  **Protozoa characteristics:** unicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic, locomotion by cilia, flagella or pseudopodia, reproduce by binary fission or multiple fission.  ·  **Classification:** (1) Mastigophora (flagella: Euglena, Trypanosoma), (2) Sarcodina (pseudopodia: Amoeba, Entamoeba), (3) Ciliophora (cilia: Paramecium, Vorticella), (4) Sporozoa (spores, parasitic: Plasmodium, Toxoplasma).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Protozoa: diagnostic features  ·  • Classification up to class with examples  ·  **Plasmodium reproduces only in mosquitoes.** — Plasmodium undergoes asexual reproduction (schizogony) extensively in the human host (liver and blood cells). Sexual reproduction (sporogony) occurs only in the mosquito vector.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **All protozoa are harmful parasites.** — Most protozoa are free-living and ecologically beneficial (e.g., Amoeba regulates bacterial populations, Euglena contributes to photosynthesis). Only a few species are parasitic (Plasmodium, Entamoeba, Trypanosoma).  ·  **Euglena is a plant or an animal.** — Euglena is neither a plant nor an animal; it is a protist with mixotrophic nutrition. It has chloroplasts for photosynthesis (plant-like) but lacks a cell wall and can also feed heterotrophically (animal-like).  ·  **Contractile vacuoles are found in all protozoa.** — Contractile vacuoles are present only in freshwater protozoa that need osmoregulation. Marine protozoa generally lack contractile vacuoles because the external environment is isotonic or hypertonic to their cytoplasm.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **The cyst stage is always the active feeding stage of a protozoan.** — The cyst stage is a dormant, non-feeding, protective stage. The trophozoite is the active, feeding, and reproducing stage. Cysts are important for survival and transmission but do not feed or grow.  ·  **All algae are protists.** — Not all algae are protists. Green algae (Chlorophyta) and red algae (Rhodophyta) are now classified in the kingdom Plantae; blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are bacteria.…  ·  **Plasmodium has flagella in its life cycle.** — Plasmodium (Sporozoa) is largely non-motile in all stages except for the microgametes (male gametes) in the mosquito gut, which are briefly flagellated.…
